paragraphs: 4Real generates dynamic 3D scenes from text, with time supplying the fourth dimension. The paper addresses a limitation of approaches built around pretrained 3D generators: their reliance on synthetic object datasets often produces object-centered scenes with limited photorealism. Its pipeline instead draws on video generators trained on diverse real-world footage, using their visual knowledge to construct scenes that can be viewed from multiple perspectives.

The process starts with a generated reference video. From that reference, the method produces a freeze-time video and learns a canonical 3D representation, which serves as the scene's shared spatial foundation. Because the freeze-time video can contain inconsistencies, the system jointly learns frame-specific deformations to account for these imperfections during reconstruction.

A further temporal deformation model captures the changing interactions in the original reference video. This separates the construction of the shared scene from the modeling of its dynamics. The paper reports improved photorealism and structural integrity, presenting video generation as a useful foundation for dynamic, explorable scenes without requiring a multi-view generative model.
neurips-2024-4real-towards-photorealisti.tldr: 4Real turns generated videos into dynamic 3D scenes by learning a shared scene representation and deformations for inconsistencies and motion.

paragraphs: Video salient object ranking asks which objects attract attention most strongly as a scene changes. The paper approaches this as a graph problem, combining spatial contrasts at multiple scales with temporal relationships within individual objects and between different objects. This gives the model several kinds of evidence for deciding how an object's visual priority should change across frames.

Its motion analysis focuses on each object individually. The model compares an object's features with features from the same spatial region in neighboring frames, rather than relying only on global comparisons between frames or proposals. The authors report that this produces more accurate motion-related saliency cues. Spatial and temporal signals are then optimized together within one graph.

That joint treatment matters because the attention ranking depends on both appearance and movement. The paper reports better dynamics than methods that process spatial cues before temporal ones, along with superior ranking results in extensive experiments. It also introduces and evaluates a video retargeting method driven by these rankings, demonstrating a practical use for the resulting attention priorities.
neurips-2024-a-motion-aware-spatio-tempo.tldr: A unified graph combines object-specific motion with spatial contrast to improve video attention ranking and support video retargeting.

paragraphs: ATAC-Diff addresses the generation and analysis of single-cell ATAC sequencing data, which researchers use to investigate differences in cellular epigenetic landscapes. Dropout during experimental amplification introduces noise and leaves the measurements extremely sparse, making analysis difficult. The paper develops one adaptable framework for multiple tasks, addressing the tendency of existing approaches to specialize in individual tasks.

The framework uses a diffusion model conditioned on auxiliary latent variables: hidden representations intended to capture higher-level information in the data. Auxiliary encoding modules, a Gaussian mixture prior, and an auxiliary decoder help these variables retain genomic information useful for downstream analysis. Conditioning generation on those representations gives the model a way to use learned semantic structure when sampling data.

A mutual-information regularizer encourages a connection between observed data and hidden variables, helping prevent the diffusion model from ignoring its conditioning information. The authors report strong results across both generation and analysis tasks, exceeding the state-of-the-art models evaluated. The contribution combines data generation with informative internal representations in a single framework.
neurips-2024-a-versatile-informative-dif.tldr: ATAC-Diff uses informative latent conditioning to support both generation and analysis of sparse single-cell ATAC sequencing data.

paragraphs: Dense object detectors can produce many false positives in complex images when their emphasis is on finding as many objects as possible. Adaptive Important Region Selection, or AIRS, addresses this by learning where to search. Inspired by visual attention, it organizes the search hierarchically, beginning with coarse regions and progressively examining selected areas at finer levels.

At each level, the model identifies patches likely to contain relevant objects and discards patches judged uninformative. Its decisions are guided by an evidential Q-learning method and a specially designed reward function. The Q-values incorporate epistemic uncertainty, meaning uncertainty associated with what the model has not yet learned, so unfamiliar regions can receive exploration attention.

This uncertainty-aware search is particularly relevant early in training, when immediately favoring familiar regions could overlook useful ones. The framework dynamically balances investigating unknown patches with revisiting regions already considered valuable. The paper presents theoretical analysis and experiments across multiple datasets supporting its reported advantage over state-of-the-art models. Its central contribution is an adaptive search policy for improving detection accuracy in difficult scenes.
neurips-2024-adaptive-important-region-s.tldr: AIRS improves dense object detection through hierarchical region selection that balances promising patches with uncertain ones.

paragraphs: This paper studies optimization with two ordered objectives. The task is to minimize an upper-level function while restricting the answer to solutions that already minimize a lower-level constrained problem. Both objectives are convex and smooth. The challenge is that the lower-level optimal solution set is itself defined by an optimization problem, making it difficult to use directly as a constraint.

The proposed method locally approximates that solution set with cutting planes and applies accelerated gradient updates to improve the upper-level objective within the approximation. Its analysis tracks two separate errors: upper-level suboptimality and lower-level infeasibility. With a compact feasible set, the iteration bound is O(max{1/sqrt(ε_f), 1/ε_g}), where the two tolerances control those respective errors.

Under an additional r-th Hölderian error-bound assumption on the lower-level objective, the paper proves a different bound: O(max{ε_f^(-(2r−1)/(2r)), ε_g^(-(2r−1)/(2r))}). At r = 1, this matches the optimal complexity of single-level convex constrained optimization. These are finite-iteration guarantees whose strength depends explicitly on the stated assumptions.
neurips-2024-an-accelerated-gradient-met.tldr: A cutting-plane and accelerated-gradient method provides explicit convergence guarantees for convex smooth bilevel optimization.

paragraphs: This paper develops a visual learning model in which top-down processing serves two purposes: carrying feedback for learning and directing vision toward a requested task or location. Existing biologically motivated models often emphasize the first role. The authors argue that integrating both roles is important for a model intended to reflect how visual processing is organized in the cortex.

Their architecture combines bottom-up and top-down streams through a particular connectivity pattern and a processing cycle that uses the top-down stream twice. A learning mechanism called Counter-Hebb operates across both streams. The paper shows that this mechanism can produce synaptic modifications exactly matching backpropagation, connecting the proposed learning scheme to an established way of training artificial networks.

The model also guides visual processing toward tasks of interest and achieves competitive results against AI models on standard multitask benchmarks. Together, these findings demonstrate that the architecture can support both learning feedback and task guidance. The authors present this combination as a possible direction for biologically plausible vision models and artificial instructed systems, including vision-language models.
neurips-2024-biologically-inspired-learn.tldr: A biologically inspired vision model unifies top-down task guidance with a learning mechanism that can reproduce backpropagation updates.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether language models can learn to omit reasoning steps while still answering correctly. The motivation comes from human expertise: practice can make some intermediate steps unnecessary to state explicitly. The authors note that language models do not inherently share human motivations to reduce effort or reasoning length, so they introduce a controlled process that actively encourages shorter solutions.

Their framework iteratively refines models toward reasoning paths that are both shorter and accurate. They then expand the training data to include a mixture of complete reasoning sequences and sequences with steps skipped. This gives fine-tuning access to both detailed solutions and more compact routes through the same kind of reasoning.

Experiments indicate that models can develop step-skipping behavior with this guidance. The trained models solve the evaluated tasks more efficiently without losing accuracy, and their out-of-domain generalization is comparable or sometimes better. These findings support learned reasoning compression in the studied settings; they connect shorter reasoning to a deliberate training process that preserves successful task performance.
neurips-2024-can-language-models-learn-t.tldr: Guided training teaches language models to use shorter reasoning paths while preserving accuracy and sometimes improving out-of-domain generalization.

paragraphs: Event streams from bio-inspired vision sensors contain spatial and temporal signals generated by motion. Separating overlapping motions is difficult when their sources and movement patterns are not known beforehand. This paper connects that task to Bayesian computation in spiking neural networks, seeking a practical application for neural processing mechanisms with physiological interpretability.

The network implements counterparts of the two stages in expectation-maximization, a framework already used for separating motion in event streams. Winner-take-all circuits perform an equivalent of the expectation step, while spike-timing-dependent plasticity, or STDP, supplies an equivalent optimization for the maximization step. This creates a link between the network's activity and learning rules and the underlying probabilistic inference procedure.

Theoretical analysis and experiments show that STDP-based learning can maximize the contrast of warped events under mixed motion models. The experiments also demonstrate that the constructed network effectively segments motion in event streams. The contribution is a concrete connection between spike-based learning, Bayesian motion separation, and the processing of continuous sensor events.
neurips-2024-continuous-spatiotemporal-e.tldr: A spiking neural network separates motions in event streams by implementing Bayesian expectation-maximization through neural competition and STDP.

paragraphs: ControlMLLM gives multimodal language models a way to focus on user-indicated image regions without retraining the model. The paper starts from the observation that attention connects text tokens with visual tokens and influences the resulting response. Its method uses this connection to steer the model toward regions specified through visual prompts.

During inference, the method adjusts visual tokens produced by the model's multilayer perceptron output. A learnable latent variable is optimized using an energy function that strengthens the indicated regions in the attention map. Here, training-free means that the model does not undergo retraining; the approach still performs optimization during inference to control how text attends to image content.

The framework accepts boxes, masks, scribbles, and points, supporting detailed descriptions and reasoning about selected regions. The reported results demonstrate out-of-domain generalization and interpretability. The approach matters because it introduces region-referring behavior through control of an existing model's attention, offering a route to visual prompting without the substantial training costs associated with learning that capability through model retraining.
neurips-2024-controlmllm-training-free-v.tldr: ControlMLLM optimizes a latent variable during inference to steer multimodal model attention toward visually prompted regions without retraining.

paragraphs: Feature attribution assigns importance to input features, but an explanation can be misleading when hidden confounders influence the relationships learned by a model. This paper focuses on faithfulness to the process that generated the data. Its concern is that attribution methods can neglect unobserved influences and consequently mix their effects with the contributions assigned to measured inputs.

The proposed approach uses instrumental variables to train what the authors describe as a confounder-free model. Its purpose is to disentangle hidden confounder effects from input features during model training. The resulting model output is aligned with the inputs' contributions to the target in the data-generating process, establishing the basis for the subsequent feature explanations.

This makes model construction part of the attribution method: the procedure changes the model whose behavior is being explained so that its outputs better reflect the intended feature contributions. The authors report more robust attributions from this data-generation perspective and demonstrate effectiveness on synthetic and real-world datasets. The stated result concerns explanations grounded in those underlying contributions.
neurips-2024-data-faithful-feature-attri.tldr: Instrumental-variable training separates hidden confounder effects from input contributions to produce more data-faithful feature attributions.

paragraphs: DEL learns three-dimensional particle dynamics from partial two-dimensional observations. Neural rendering makes this possible by connecting simulated 3D configurations to images, but the inverse problem is ambiguous: different particle arrangements can explain the same image. The paper addresses this uncertainty by building a learned simulator around an established mechanical framework.

The architecture extends Discrete Element Analysis with learnable graph kernels. These graph networks approximate particular mechanical operators within the framework, leaving the broader organization of the dynamics grounded in physical structure. This focuses learning on selected components of the simulation and supplies a mechanically interpretable prior for reconstructing dynamics from incomplete visual evidence.

The authors report that this combination learns the dynamics of different materials within a unified approach. In the setting of partial 2D supervision, experiments show a large advantage over other learned simulators. They also demonstrate robustness across renderers and when training samples or camera views are reduced. The results support incorporating strong mechanical structure when visual observations leave the underlying 3D dynamics uncertain.
neurips-2024-del-discrete-element-learne.tldr: DEL combines mechanical simulation structure with learned graph operators to recover 3D particle dynamics from partial 2D observations.

paragraphs: This paper estimates fluid motion by tracking three-dimensional particles between two consecutive frames, a central step in particle tracking velocimetry. Deep learning methods have achieved strong accuracy for this task but depend heavily on labeled training data. The authors introduce a fully self-supervised approach and report that it exceeds fully supervised counterparts using only 1% as many training samples, without labels.

A central component is a zero-divergence loss tailored to turbulent flow. This provides a domain-specific constraint for learning from the observations themselves. The paper introduces a splat-based implementation designed to make that loss efficient and effective, connecting the physical training objective to a practical computational procedure.

Because its learning objective does not require labels, the method can also optimize on test data. A dedicated Dynamic Velocimetry Enhancer module supports this adaptation. Experiments report strong cross-domain robustness on held-out synthetic domains and real physical and biological domains. The findings connect reduced dependence on labeled data with the ability to adjust motion estimates to unfamiliar conditions at inference.
neurips-2024-dual-frame-fluid-motion-est.tldr: A self-supervised fluid motion estimator combines zero-divergence loss with test-time optimization, outperforming supervised counterparts with 1% as many training samples.

paragraphs: Unsupervised domain adaptation aims to transfer a model across domains without labeled target-domain data. The paper addresses a tension in learning features that are shared across domains: enforcing invariance can interfere with retaining distinctions useful for prediction. Prompt-based adaptation of pretrained vision-language models provides a way to learn both shared and domain-specific information.

The authors formulate adaptation as a multiple-objective problem, assigning a loss to each domain. Their method aligns the gradients of these objectives so that the updates they request are more consistent with one another. It also penalizes gradient norms to help prevent potential overfitting during fine-tuning. A practical update procedure supports both single-source and multiple-source adaptation.

This approach places the coordination mechanism in the optimization process, where domain objectives determine how prompts are updated. The paper reports consistent improvements by a large margin over other vision-language adaptation methods across a wide range of benchmarks. These empirical findings support gradient agreement as a useful way to coordinate domain learning while preserving the flexibility of prompt-based adaptation.
neurips-2024-enhancing-domain-adaptation.tldr: Aligning domain-loss gradients improves prompt-based domain adaptation while gradient-norm penalties help control potential overfitting.

paragraphs: The Segment Anything Model can produce substantially different segmentations after small prompt changes, including changes in how finely an object is divided. This paper examines that sensitivity in settings where the data themselves admit multiple reasonable labels. In such cases, diversity in segmentation can be useful if it reflects the ambiguity in the labeling task and can be controlled.

The authors introduce an optimization framework based on a conditional variational autoencoder. It jointly represents the prompt and object granularity through a latent probability distribution. That distribution lets the framework model alternative segmentation interpretations and guide SAM toward a range of plausible outputs associated with the ambiguous data.

The intended result is controlled diversity: a series of convincing segmentations that represents the underlying label distribution. Experiments across several practical scenarios involving ambiguity demonstrate strong performance for the framework. The contribution is to make SAM's sensitivity useful for modeling legitimate variation in labels, linking prompt variation and segmentation granularity through a learned probabilistic representation.
neurips-2024-flaws-can-be-applause-unlea.tldr: A conditional variational framework turns SAM's prompt sensitivity into controlled, diverse segmentations for inherently ambiguous objects.

paragraphs: FreqBlender creates synthetic fake faces for training DeepFake detectors. Existing approaches often build these examples by blending faces in image space, but the paper argues that this leaves their frequency distributions insufficiently modeled. That omission can limit how deeply a detector learns forgery traces that generalize beyond particular training examples.

The method introduces a Frequency Parsing Network that adaptively separates frequency components associated with forgery traces. It then blends this frequency information from fake faces into real faces to produce training examples. The aim is to make the generated examples carry useful frequency-level evidence of manipulation, extending the information supplied by conventional spatial blending.

There are no ground-truth labels for the desired frequency components, so the authors develop a training strategy based on internal relationships among different kinds of frequency information. Experiments demonstrate improved DeepFake detection. The authors describe the approach as a potential plug-and-play addition to other methods, positioning frequency-based synthesis as a way to strengthen training data for detection.
neurips-2024-freqblender-enhancing-deepf.tldr: FreqBlender improves DeepFake detector training by blending learned forgery-related frequency information from fake faces into real ones.

paragraphs: Task Adapters Generation from Instructions, or TAGI, targets situations where a language model must handle new tasks with few labeled examples available. Standard instruction fine-tuning still depends heavily on training instances. TAGI instead learns to use a task's instructions to generate task-specific adapter parameters, allowing it to construct an adapted model for an unseen task without retraining on that task.

The framework learns this capability through hypernetwork pretraining followed by fine-tuning. Knowledge distillation connects instruction-based generation with models trained on task examples. Specifically, training aligns labels, output logits, and adapter parameters, so the instruction-generated model is encouraged to behave consistently with a model developed through instance training.

Evaluations on Super-Natural Instructions and P3 show that TAGI can match or exceed traditional meta-trained models and other hypernetwork approaches while substantially reducing computational requirements. The result supports learning a reusable mapping from task descriptions to model parameters. Its cross-task capability comes from the two-stage training process, which prepares the system to generate adapters when new instructions arrive.
neurips-2024-from-instance-training-to-i.tldr: TAGI learns to generate task-specific adapters from instructions, supporting unseen tasks without task-specific retraining.

paragraphs: Stochastic compositional optimization concerns problems with an outer function applied to an inner function under uncertainty. Such problems arise in areas including risk management, reinforcement learning, and meta-learning. Many existing methods assume both functions are smooth. This paper broadens the setting to functions that are Lipschitz continuous but can each be nonconvex and nonsmooth.

The authors propose stochastic methods that do not require gradients. Their theoretical target is a (δ, ε)-Goldstein stationary point, an approximate stationarity criterion suited to nonsmooth problems. They establish non-asymptotic convergence rates, giving finite-run guarantees for approaching that criterion. Because the setting includes nonconvex functions, these results concern stationarity rather than a guarantee of finding a global optimum.

The analysis also yields an improved convergence rate for the convex nonsmooth version of the problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The contribution therefore combines a broader set of admissible objectives with explicit convergence guarantees, allowing both layers of the composition to lack the smoothness required by much earlier work.
neurips-2024-gradient-free-methods-for-n.tldr: Gradient-free stochastic methods provide finite-run stationarity guarantees when both layers of a compositional objective can be nonconvex and nonsmooth.

paragraphs: Graph autoencoders compress nodes into embeddings and use those embeddings to reconstruct a graph's connections. This paper investigates limitations of the self-correlation mechanisms commonly used for reconstruction. Its theoretical analysis finds that these mechanisms generally struggle to represent features such as isolated graph regions, symmetric structures, and directed edges, especially for small graphs or collections of multiple graphs.

The proposed alternative uses cross-correlation to expand what the reconstruction mechanism can represent. GraphCroc incorporates this idea into an autoencoder with a mirrored encoding and decoding process. It supports flexible encoder architectures for different downstream tasks and adds a loss-balancing strategy to address representation bias that can arise during optimization.

These changes address both representational capacity and how that capacity is learned. The paper provides theoretical analysis and numerical evaluations showing substantially better structural reconstruction than existing self-correlation-based graph autoencoders. Its emphasis on smaller and multiple-graph settings also broadens the focus beyond the node-level tasks that have dominated much of the prior work discussed in the abstract.
neurips-2024-graphcroc-cross-correlation.tldr: GraphCroc improves graph reconstruction by replacing self-correlation with cross-correlation and balancing the reconstruction loss.

paragraphs: HairFast transfers a hairstyle from a reference image onto an input photograph for virtual try-on. The task must handle differences in pose while preserving convincing hair shape and color. The paper identifies a practical tradeoff in existing methods: optimization-based approaches are slow, while faster encoder-based systems can deliver poor quality. Large pose differences create additional difficulties.

The proposed architecture operates in StyleGAN's FS latent space and combines several targeted components. These include enhanced inpainting, improved encoders for alignment and color transfer, and a new post-processing encoder. Together, they support high-resolution output and near-real-time operation, with the authors reporting better reconstruction than optimization-based methods.

The evaluation examines realism after random hairstyle transfers and reconstruction when the original hairstyle is transferred back. For the difficult setting where hairstyle shape and color come from different images, the method completes the transfer in under one second on an Nvidia V100. This ties the speed claim to a specific hardware setting while demonstrating an approach designed to address quality and pose alignment together.
neurips-2024-hairfastgan-realistic-and-r.tldr: HairFast combines StyleGAN FS-space encoding, alignment, and inpainting for realistic hairstyle transfer in under a second on an Nvidia V100.

paragraphs: TABULA-8B brings large-scale transfer learning to spreadsheet-style prediction tasks. The authors build a filtered, quality-controlled training collection from TabLib containing more than 2.1 billion rows from 4.2 million unique tables. They use it to fine-tune Llama 3-8B for classification and binned regression, with a new packing and attention scheme designed for tabular prediction.

The central question is whether training across many tables can produce useful predictions on previously unseen ones. Across a test suite of 329 datasets, TABULA-8B achieves zero-shot accuracy more than 15 percentage points above random guessing. The paper reports this as a capability unavailable to the existing tabular predictors considered, including XGBoost and TabPFN.

With 1–32 examples and no fine-tuning on target datasets, TABULA-8B is reported to be 5–15 percentage points more accurate than XGBoost and TabPFN trained on equal amounts of data or even up to 16 times more. These results support transferring prediction knowledge across tables, particularly when target-specific examples are scarce. The authors also release the model, code, and data.
neurips-2024-large-scale-transfer-learni.tldr: TABULA-8B learns across millions of tables to deliver strong zero-shot and few-shot predictions on unseen tabular datasets.

paragraphs: This paper studies learning linear decision boundaries when the data have a margin and labels are corrupted by Massart noise. The margin parameter γ measures the separation assumed in the learning problem. Massart noise is a more demanding setting than random classification noise, so guarantees that work only for random corruption do not cover the full problem considered here.

The authors introduce Perspectron, a simple proper learning algorithm, meaning that its learned classifier remains a halfspace. It achieves classification error at most η + ε, where η is the Massart noise rate and ε is the additional allowed error. Its sample complexity is approximately 1/(εγ)², with logarithmic factors suppressed by the stated bound.

This improves earlier guarantees in their dependence on accuracy and margin, while accommodating the stronger noise model. The paper also extends the results to generalized linear models under Massart noise, provided the link function is known, with similar sample complexity. The contribution concerns efficient learning under those explicit margin and noise conditions, together with a stronger result for the stated generalized model.
neurips-2024-learning-noisy-halfspaces-w.tldr: Perspectron improves sample guarantees for learning margin-separated halfspaces under Massart noise and extends to generalized linear models with known links.

paragraphs: R²-Gaussian adapts 3D Gaussian splatting to sparse-view tomography, where a volume must be reconstructed from a limited collection of X-ray views. Although Gaussian splatting has shown promise for rendering images and reconstructing surfaces, recovering an entire volume poses a different challenge. The authors derive X-ray rasterization functions and identify an integration bias in the standard formulation that interferes with accurate volume recovery.

Their correction changes how three-dimensional Gaussians are projected into two dimensions. The framework combines Gaussian kernels tailored to the task, rasterization extended to X-ray imaging, and a CUDA-based differentiable voxelizer. These components connect the corrected Gaussian representation to volumetric reconstruction while supporting efficient computation.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world data report better accuracy and efficiency than state-of-the-art approaches. The method produces high-quality reconstructions in four minutes, reported as 12 times faster than NeRF-based methods and comparable in speed to traditional algorithms. The key finding is that correcting the projection's integration behavior makes Gaussian splatting useful for fast reconstruction of volumetric information.
neurips-2024-r-2-gaussian-rectifying-rad.tldr: R²-Gaussian corrects an integration bias in Gaussian splatting to deliver accurate sparse-view tomographic reconstructions in four minutes.

paragraphs: This paper studies linear classification when one kind of mistake is more costly than another. It uses the reliable agnostic PAC framework and assumes Gaussian-distributed inputs in d dimensions. The distinction from standard agnostic learning is consequential: the learner must meet the reliability objective, so its computational requirements need to be analyzed under that stronger learning framework.

The authors give a new algorithm with explicit sample and computational complexity bounds. These depend on the dimension d, the excess-error tolerance ε, and the bias α of the optimal halfspace. In the dimensional factor, the exponent grows logarithmically with the smaller of 1/α and 1/ε; additional factors depend on the accuracy and bias parameters.

A complementary Statistical Query lower bound suggests that dimensional dependence of the form d raised to a constant multiple of log(1/α) is unavoidable in that framework. This lower bound has the stated Statistical Query scope. Together, the results establish a strong computational separation between reliable and standard agnostic halfspace learning under Gaussian inputs.
neurips-2024-reliable-learning-of-halfsp.tldr: New upper and Statistical Query lower bounds reveal a strong computational separation between reliable and standard agnostic Gaussian halfspace learning.

paragraphs: The Well is a collection of physics simulation datasets intended to improve how researchers train and evaluate machine-learning surrogate models. These models can accelerate simulation-based work, but datasets covering only narrow classes of physical behavior make it difficult to judge new methods broadly. The Well addresses that evaluation gap by bringing together simulations of many systems that evolve through space and time.

The collection contains 15 terabytes across 16 datasets, assembled with contributions from domain experts and numerical software developers. Its scope includes biological systems, fluid dynamics, acoustic scattering, and magnetohydrodynamic simulations involving extragalactic fluids or supernova explosions. Researchers can work with individual datasets or combine them into a broader benchmark suite.

A unified PyTorch interface supports model training and evaluation across the collection. The authors also provide example baselines that demonstrate the library and highlight challenges created by its complex dynamics. The contribution is both a substantial shared data resource and a common access layer, making diverse physical prediction problems available within a consistent workflow.
neurips-2024-the-well-a-large-scale-coll.tldr: The Well provides 15 terabytes of diverse physics simulations across 16 datasets with a unified interface for machine-learning evaluation.

paragraphs: Boltzmann Generators learn to produce equilibrium samples of molecular systems by transforming a simple probability distribution into a target Boltzmann distribution. This paper extends work that trains such generators using flow matching in Cartesian coordinates. Its goal is transfer across chemical space: a trained generator should make predictions for new molecules without being retrained separately for each molecular system.

The proposed framework provides approximate samples for unseen systems and supports efficient reweighting to the target Boltzmann distribution. That distinction matters because direct generated samples are described as approximate, while reweighting supplies a way to account for their relationship to the desired distribution. The intended benefit is reuse of a learned generator across molecular systems.

The authors evaluate transferability on dipeptides and report efficient generalization to unseen systems within that evaluation. They also show that the proposed architecture improves the efficiency of generators trained for individual molecular systems. The findings therefore support both a transferable sampling framework and an architectural improvement for the single-system setting, with the transfer evidence grounded in dipeptide experiments.
neurips-2024-transferable-boltzmann-gene.tldr: Transferable Boltzmann Generators approximately sample unseen molecular systems without retraining and support efficient reweighting to their target distributions.
